expectations.text: Models at least one negative-spillover scenario per shortlisted candidate and what it would cost Solane
expectations.evidence: No candidate is actually shortlisted (every row is 'Not ranked'), so the per-candidate requirement is never discharged. For the two named candidates there are only gestures at spillover, not modeled scenarios with costs: Halvern gets 'reduced brand esteem on average for the higher-esteem partner' (framed as Halvern's exposure, not Solane's), 'asymmetric-prestige/dilution watch', and an exclusivity clause that 'may lock you out of adjacent-category partnerships for the term, which is a real cost' — the cost is asserted, never sized or traced (no lost-partnership, revenue, or positioning consequ

expectations.evidence: Only two of eleven candidates get any spillover reasoning, and the response explicitly refuses to produce a shortlist at all ('I can't produce a real ranking yet'), so there is no set of shortlisted candidates with per-candidate downside modeling. Where it does engage: Halvern gets a genuine spillover scenario ('junior-partner effect — you look like the brand reaching up... your 95€-basket positioning gets diluted rather than elevated'), which is the strongest item here.
